task.name: A broken baseline blocks every sprint and can only be cleared by hand, though forge has already reproduced and captured the failure
task.story_text:
## What

Let a broken baseline be routed into forge's own dev and review pipeline, so the
operator can clear it with a command instead of editing files by hand.

## Why

When the configured gate fails on a sprint's merge base, forge aborts before any dev
work and every story in the sprint is refused. That refusal is correct — running stories
against a base that cannot pass its own gate would attribute the breakage to whichever
story landed next.

The gap is what happens afterward. Forge has already done the expensive part: it ran the
gate, reproduced the failure on an immediate re-run to rule out flake, captured the full
output, and preserved a worktree pinned at the failing merge base. That is a better
starting point than most issues forge accepts. It then stops, and the only way forward is
a human opening the gate log, finding the failing target, writing the fix, and landing it
through a separate branch and PR.

Writing a fix from a reproduced failure is the thing forge does. Requiring it to be done
by hand means the one condition that blocks *all* sprints is also the one condition forge
cannot help with, and it recurs: a project accumulates clock-dependent tests, generated
files that exist only in a developer checkout, and environment assumptions that surface
first in a clean baseline worktree — none of which the authoring story's own gate catches,
because that gate ran somewhere the assumption held.

Observed twice in four days on one project. Both times every queued sprint was blocked
until a person fixed the baseline manually; both fixes were small and mechanical once the
gate output was read.

## Acceptance criteria

- An operator can direct a reproduced baseline failure into forge's dev and review
  pipeline with a single command, without hand-editing files to unblock sprints.
- The work item forge derives from the failure carries what the abort already captured:
  the gate output, the failing target, and the preserved reproduction worktree.
- A baseline fix lands through the same gate and review path as any other change, with no
  special-cased merge or reduced review.
- Where forge cannot produce a fix, it reports that and leaves the reproduction intact
  rather than retrying or discarding it.

## Example

A sprint aborts:

```
RuntimeError: Broken baseline: configured gate failed on sprint merge base f0465b67
before any dev work started (Gate returned FAIL) (failure reproduced on an immediate
re-run of the identical gate)
Full gate output: .forge/logs/issues-358,357,356,355/run-4eee22b47abd-baseline-gate.txt
Baseline worktree preserved for reproduction: .forge/forge-baseline-hp4sahuz/worktree
```

The gate output names the failure precisely:

```
FAILED tests/test_storage_invariants.py::test_lab_surfaces_agree_per_result
  AssertionError: missing from the lake: [(1, date(2026,5,24), 'Quest', 'Ferritin'), ...]
                  missing from the live table: [(1, date(2026,5,25), 'Quest', 'Ferritin'), ...]
```

The cause was a fixture generating dates from `datetime.now()` compared against dates
hardcoded the previous day — a one-line class of fix, found by reading the output forge
had already written. Today that reading and fixing is entirely manual; the failing target,
the assertion, and a worktree that reproduces it were all already in hand.

## Notes

`--force` bypasses the sprint-entry shape gate and does not apply here. Bypassing the
baseline gate is not what this asks for: running stories on a knowingly broken base is the
outcome the gate exists to prevent, and the fix should land before the sprint proceeds, not
alongside it.

Authoritative gate verdict was UNAVAILABLE, so I ran targeted suites (test_baseline_repair, test_cli_baseline_fix, test_sprint_baseline_gate, test_issue_body_producer_conformance, convention tests) plus ruff — all pass; three P2s on run bootstrap, audit-selection ambiguity semantics, and a missing writer→reader seam test.

findings.description: A baseline-fix run invokes the coordinator without publishing the run context that every other run entry point publishes, so no run id or project root is exported and the agent subprocesses it spawns are never registered in the .forge/runs/agents sidecar directory, leaving the run invisible to forge status and its agent process groups outside the orphan sweep.

With no selector flag the command treats the newest per-run sprint audit as unambiguous unless a second audit shares its modification timestamp to the nanosecond, so in practice a stale or unrelated sprint audit is selected silently while the operator-facing docs state that the default only selects the latest audit when the choice is unambiguous.

Both new test modules feed the repair reader hand-authored sprint-audit YAML rather than a record produced by the sprint's own audit writer, so nothing exercises the seam where the baseline gate's captured fields are serialised into the audit and read back by the repair path.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 3 proposes manually constructing TaskStory from the issue number and body. Unless it also populates type, fix_ready, and investigation_ready, it bypasses metadata derived by GitHubIssueSource.fetch in src/theforge/sprint/sources.py. That would omit the investigation-ready guidance in task/dev_prompts.py and the bug-specific symptom-test escalation in coordinator/review_phase.py.
  Suggestion: After creating the issue, load it through GitHubIssueSource.fetch, or explicitly derive and populate the same structured bug metadata before calling run_task.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 3 does not state how the command selects a landing-capable disposition. run_task defaults auto_merge to false, while WorkspaceConfig defaults on_approve to none, so an approved run can finish with an unlanded branch even though the command is intended to clear the baseline.
  Suggestion: Define and test the command's landing behavior explicitly: forward an operator flag such as --auto-merge or fail early unless workspace.on_approve is merge or merge-pr, and pass the same effective setting to _write_audit.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 does not state how the fix actually lands. run_task's auto_merge defaults to False, so without specifying it the command would produce an approved-but-unlanded fix and sprints would remain blocked on the same broken base — the single-command unblock in AC1 depends on this.
  Suggestion: Pick the landing contract explicitly in Step 3: pass auto_merge (or expose a --merge flag mirroring cmd_run's) and pass lands_in_project_root/base_lands_locally consistently with the standalone-run defaults, so the fix lands through the ordinary gate/review path.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 constructs TaskStory from the created issue but does not set type (or fix_ready), which GitHubIssueSource normally populates from labels; the audit (coordinator/audit.py:758) and any type-conditioned dev/preflight routing will see a typeless story even though the issue is labeled bug.
  Suggestion: Set type='bug' on the constructed TaskStory (and fix_ready appropriately, since the rendered body carries a reproduced failure and evidence), or reuse GitHubIssueSource's task-construction path for the created issue number instead of hand-building the dataclass.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2's guard requires baseline_check.failure_reproduced == true, but the abort at runner.py:5417 fires on any passed false record — including the early error returns (no git checkout toplevel, merge-base failure, worktree setup failure) that never set failure_reproduced and have no worktree/evidence to route.
  Suggestion: Have the loader distinguish 'not a reproduced gate failure' from 'malformed audit' and print which precondition failed (missing failure_reproduced, missing worktree, worktree pruned by _prune_preserved_baseline_worktrees) so the operator sees why routing was refused.

finding_registry.description: A baseline-fix run invokes the coordinator without publishing the run context that every other run entry point publishes, so no run id or project root is exported and the agent subprocesses it spawns are never registered in the .forge/runs/agents sidecar directory, leaving the run invisible to forge status and its agent process groups outside the orphan sweep.

With no selector flag the command treats the newest per-run sprint audit as unambiguous unless a second audit shares its modification timestamp to the nanosecond, so in practice a stale or unrelated sprint audit is selected silently while the operator-facing docs state that the default only selects the latest audit when the choice is unambiguous.

Both new test modules feed the repair reader hand-authored sprint-audit YAML rather than a record produced by the sprint's own audit writer, so nothing exercises the seam where the baseline gate's captured fields are serialised into the audit and read back by the repair path.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
